sections.gov_regulatory:
- Non-clinical wellness tool today — no diagnostic/treatment claim; danger-sign triage is done by a human ANM, not software.
- Classification is live, not fixed: PRAMS, SORS, and WHO Risk Score are already collected in DHIS2.
- Switching on automated triage against those scores is named as the organisation's highest-value next act — which would reopen the classification question toward Class IIa clinical decision support.
- Named gap: Nepal has no regulatory sandbox or SaMD classification framework.
- Named gap: no ISO 13485/IEC 62304/ISO 14971 certification is evidenced.
sections.gov_clinical:
- Danger signs are triaged by a human on the counselling line, not automatically — automated detection without a referral pathway is judged unsafe.
- The same logic has kept mental-health screening and automated risk-score triage switched off.
- Named gap: no single national maternal/newborn protocol repository to cite as 'the governing protocol' (no PNPK-equivalent in Nepal).
- Named gap: no adverse-event/near-miss reporting pathway is evidenced in the organisation's own records.
sections.gov_data:
- Stated policy: mother data is available only to the DHO, Government of Nepal, and the related health post/management — never publicly available, treated as a founding value.
- Named gap: Nepal's closest law is the general Individual Privacy Act, 2075 (2018); there is no health-sector-specific data protection law, so this commitment currently rests on internal policy, not a health-data statute.
- Named gap: consent-capture process is not formally documented.
- Named gap: end-of-project data fate is not formally documented.
sections.gov_tech:
- Counselling programme runs on the national DHIS2-based platform (19,699 enrolled, 160 data elements, 27 indicators), not a standalone database.
- Four-tier access model (mother/FCHV/health post/DHO), with scoped third-party access for at least one partner.
- Organisation separately holds FHIR R5 work (16 profiles, hmis.gov.np/fhir) at company level, but this product's own consumption of it is not evidenced.
- Offline-first by design (historically micro-SD/shared-device distribution).
- Named gap: no evidenced disaster-recovery/business-continuity policy for the platform side.
